Chapter 01 · Foundation

Chapter 01 — What does a system administrator do?

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Identify the responsibilities of someone who keeps a computer useful, secure and recoverable.

Why this matters

A system administrator keeps computers and services dependable for the people who rely on them. That may mean setting up an account for a new colleague, explaining why an application will not launch, checking whether a disk is nearly full, confirming that a backup can be restored, or investigating unusual activity. A household computer needs the same principles on a smaller scale. A school computer room, a charity office and a bank apply them to more people and higher consequences.

Administration is not the same as programming. A developer changes how software works. An administrator installs, configures, monitors and protects the environment where software runs. The roles overlap: a Umicom contributor who compiles a C23 application also needs to understand storage, permissions, running processes and logs.

A useful professional habit is to separate observation from change. Looking at free disk space is observation. Deleting old files is a change. Before a change, know what system it affects, what success looks like, how you could undo it and whether you are authorised to perform it.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
System The computer, its operating system, installed software, data, users and connected services.
Service A program that supplies a capability, often without a visible window.
Availability Whether people can use the service when they need it.
Backup A separate recoverable copy of data.
Least privilege Having only the access needed for a task.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Open PowerShell and ask where you are

Get-Location

Expected observation: A path is displayed. You have observed the current folder, not changed it.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Identify the signed-in account

whoami

Expected observation: Windows prints the account under which the command is running.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — List the visible files

Get-ChildItem

Expected observation: A list is returned or nothing is shown for an empty directory.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Ask which account is running

whoami

Expected observation: The current account name appears.

Linux step 2 — Show current folder

pwd

Expected observation: Linux prints the current path.

Worked support scenario

A teacher reports that an application cannot save assignments. Do not immediately reinstall it. First confirm the affected account, the path being saved to, the free space, and the error message. Record whether another document can be saved in a safe training folder. Only then select a corrective action. This is a miniature incident investigation, not guesswork.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Changing settings before gathering evidence Write down the symptom and inspect the environment first.
Assuming administrator access is always required Begin with an ordinary account; elevation is a separate decision.
Treating a successful program launch as proof everything works Verify the real user task, such as saving and reopening a file.

Exercise: demonstrate understanding

  1. Write down the purpose of two commands from this chapter, in your own words.
  2. Run a read-only command and record only the information needed to answer its question.
  3. Explain which command would change the machine, if any, and why the chapter avoids it.
  4. Explain the difference between an observation, a conclusion and an unverified assumption.

Review questions

  1. What is the difference between observing and changing a system?
  2. Why should an administrator have a recovery plan?
Show the suggested answers
  1. Observation collects evidence; a change alters the system state.
  2. Changes can cause unintended effects, and recovery limits data loss and downtime.

How this connects to Umicom

For Umicom Studio, observation means checking the current build, logs and user workspace before editing Framework source. For Umicom OS, the distinction is even stronger: a successful boot does not prove that every user-space service is healthy.

Chapter 02 · Foundation

Chapter 02 — Understand the computer, operating system and user account

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Explain hardware, the operating system, applications and accounts as separate layers.

Why this matters

A computer has physical components such as a processor, memory, a drive and a network interface. The operating system coordinates these components and supplies standard services. Applications use those services to open files, display windows, send network requests and use memory. Your user account controls the identity and permissions under which an application acts.

It helps to picture the layers from bottom to top: hardware, operating-system kernel and drivers, operating-system services, applications and the person using them. If a text editor cannot save a document, the cause may be inside the editor, a directory permission, a full drive or a read-only file. One symptom can have several possible causes.

Windows and Linux organise these concepts differently. Windows normally shows drives such as C: and uses backslashes in paths. Linux usually presents a single directory tree rooted at /. Neither choice tells you whether a file is safe to delete. Always inspect the actual path and ownership first.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
CPU Processor that executes instructions.
RAM Working memory used while programs run.
Storage Persistent space for files and installed software.
Kernel Privileged part of the operating system that controls hardware and processes.
Account Identity whose access rights are checked by the operating system.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Show basic OS details

Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object WindowsProductName, OsVersion, OsArchitecture

Expected observation: Windows returns values describing the installed operating system.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Show the current PowerShell version

$PSVersionTable.PSVersion

Expected observation: A table-like version value appears; version 7 or higher identifies PowerShell 7.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Show your home folder

$HOME

Expected observation: You see the folder assigned to your account.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Ask Linux which kernel is running

uname -sr

Expected observation: The kernel name and release are printed.

Linux step 2 — Display account and groups

id

Expected observation: Your user ID and group memberships are shown.

Worked support scenario

Imagine a finance reporting application closes unexpectedly. A support record should state the operating system, application version, account affected and whether the problem reproduces on another account. “The computer is broken” is not specific enough to decide whether a hardware, application or permission fix is appropriate.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Confusing memory with disk space RAM is temporary working storage; disk space is persistent file storage.
Assuming all PowerShell versions are the same Check $PSVersionTable.PSVersion rather than relying on an icon.
Confusing the kernel with every program running on the machine The kernel provides services; most applications execute in user space.

Exercise: demonstrate understanding

  1. Write down the purpose of two commands from this chapter, in your own words.
  2. Run a read-only command and record only the information needed to answer its question.
  3. Explain which command would change the machine, if any, and why the chapter avoids it.
  4. Explain the difference between an observation, a conclusion and an unverified assumption.

Review questions

  1. Why can a full drive prevent an application from saving?
  2. Does changing a user account alter the CPU?
Show the suggested answers
  1. The operating system cannot allocate enough persistent storage for the file.
  2. No. The account changes identity and permissions, not the physical processor.

How this connects to Umicom

Umicom Kernel owns privileged hardware and process boundaries. Umicom OS coordinates an operating environment; Umicom Framework provides reusable user-space services; an application such as Studio consumes those contracts.

Chapter 03 · Foundation

Chapter 03 — Open PowerShell 7 or the Linux terminal without confusion

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Identify the program you have opened before typing unfamiliar commands.

Why this matters

The screenshot below is from the supplied Windows search example. It shows why the programme name and version matter more than the colour of the icon.

The Start menu can show Windows PowerShell, Windows PowerShell ISE, PowerShell and Developer PowerShell for Visual Studio. They are not identical products. Windows Terminal is the tabbed terminal application. It can host different command-line shells. PowerShell 7 is a modern shell normally launched using pwsh. Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the older Windows-included shell, normally launched with powershell.exe. CMD runs Command Prompt commands, which sometimes resemble PowerShell commands but do not share all syntax.

Your screenshot illustrates this confusion well: it shows several similar blue terminal icons in the Windows search results. To avoid mistakes, use the program name and verify the running version inside the shell. Windows PowerShell can be useful for installing PowerShell 7 when the latter is not yet available. There is no need to open a privileged shell for the exercises in this course.

A terminal window is a way to communicate with the shell. The shell reads a command, invokes a built-in operation or an external program, and displays the result. A command is not automatically a script. We use individual interactive PowerShell commands for learning and administration; all new Umicom executable implementations remain in C23 or Assembly.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Terminal A window that hosts one or more command-line sessions.
Shell Program that interprets command text.
Prompt Text that shows the shell is ready for a new command.
pwsh Executable name typically used to launch PowerShell 7.
ISE Legacy Windows PowerShell integrated scripting environment, not PowerShell 7.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Ask which version is actually running

$PSVersionTable.PSVersion

Expected observation: The Major value should be 7 when using PowerShell 7.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Ask where the executable is installed

Get-Command pwsh -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, Source

Expected observation: If available, the result identifies the executable path.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Check the current directory before continuing

Get-Location

Expected observation: The working directory is shown without changing files.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Open Terminal from the applications menu

pwd

Expected observation: The shell prints the active directory.

Linux step 2 — Identify the current shell

printf "%s\n" "$SHELL"

Expected observation: A login-shell path appears, such as /bin/bash, though the actual running shell can differ.

Worked support scenario

A contributor tries a command from a Windows tutorial in Command Prompt and receives “not recognised”. Instead of repeating it with administrator permissions, check whether the tutorial says PowerShell, CMD or Linux Bash. Launch the expected shell and verify it using its own version command.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Selecting Windows PowerShell ISE thinking it is PowerShell 7 Start pwsh or the PowerShell 7 application instead.
Typing example output as if it is a command Only type the contents of clearly labelled command blocks.
Copying PS C:\...> prompt symbols into a command Type only what comes after the prompt.

Exercise: demonstrate understanding

  1. Write down the purpose of two commands from this chapter, in your own words.
  2. Run a read-only command and record only the information needed to answer its question.
  3. Explain which command would change the machine, if any, and why the chapter avoids it.
  4. Explain the difference between an observation, a conclusion and an unverified assumption.

Review questions

  1. Is Windows Terminal the same thing as PowerShell?
  2. What command verifies your PowerShell edition and version?
Show the suggested answers
  1. No. It is a terminal host; PowerShell is a shell running inside it.
  2. $PSVersionTable.PSVersion.

How this connects to Umicom

Use PowerShell 7 for Windows contributor commands. On Linux use your preferred terminal and Bash. Do not add .ps1 or .py scripts to Umicom merely to automate tasks already implemented in Framework.

Chapter 04 · Foundation

Chapter 04 — Read a command, its arguments and the help system

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Understand the pieces of a command and find trusted documentation.

Why this matters

A command normally contains a command name followed by arguments or options. In Get-ChildItem -Path "$HOME", Get-ChildItem is the operation and -Path is the name of a parameter. The quoted folder is the value of that parameter. In git --version, --version is an option recognised by Git, not a PowerShell parameter. Different programs have different option styles.

PowerShell commands are called cmdlets when they follow the verb-noun naming convention, such as Get-Process and Test-Path. It also runs native executables such as git.exe and cmake.exe. A vertical bar | passes output to another command; you can use it to select columns rather than read pages of detail.

Before using an unfamiliar command, prefer Get-Help, the program’s --help output and its official documentation. Treat copied commands from chats and websites as proposals to review, not instructions to execute blindly. If an option looks like it deletes, formats, force-pushes or rewrites history, do not execute it during a beginner exercise.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Parameter Named input to a command, such as -Path.
Argument A value passed to a command or executable.
Pipeline A connection that passes command output to another command.
Alias An alternate name, such as pwd for Get-Location in PowerShell.
Exit code A number indicating whether a native program succeeded.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Read help for a safe command

Get-Help Get-Location -Examples

Expected observation: PowerShell displays examples and descriptions.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — See what a command actually resolves to

Get-Command pwd

Expected observation: The alias target should identify Get-Location.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Select a few columns rather than pages of data

Get-Process | Select-Object -First 5 Name, Id

Expected observation: Five process names and IDs are displayed.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Ask Git for its available options

git --help

Expected observation: Git opens or displays its help; exit any pager or viewer to return to PowerShell.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Read short help for a program

git --version

Expected observation: The Git version number appears if Git is installed.

Linux step 2 — Show the first few processes

ps -e | head -n 6

Expected observation: You see a short process list; no process is changed.

Worked support scenario

You encounter a command showing git reset --hard in an online answer. Read its help and identify that it can discard working-tree edits. Because a safer read-only observation such as git status is available, do not run the reset. Choosing the correct command is part of administration.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Typing spaces inside a single option Use --version, not - - version.
Assuming Git options and PowerShell parameters are interchangeable Consult the help for the specific command.
Assuming an empty output is always success Check the command purpose and any error output; for native processes inspect $LASTEXITCODE when appropriate.

  1. What does the pipe operator do in a PowerShell pipeline?
  2. Why should you inspect help before using reset or force flags?
Show the suggested answers
  1. It passes objects from one command to another.

How this connects to Umicom

Read CMake, Git and the built native umicom command help separately. They are different programs invoked from the same PowerShell prompt.

Chapter 05 · Foundation

Chapter 05 — Folders, file paths and your own safe practice workspace

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Create a private training directory and understand absolute and relative paths.

Why this matters

A folder groups files and other folders. The working directory is the location where relative paths are interpreted. An absolute Windows path such as C:\Users\Alex\UmicomLearning identifies a location without depending on where you started. A relative path such as notes\README.md begins inside the current directory. You can get unexpected results if you change files while standing in the wrong location.

We deliberately use $HOME\UmicomLearning for examples. $HOME is your account’s personal home folder, so the exercise does not touch your real C:\umicom\Umicom-Applications workspace or require administrator privileges. $HOME expands to a path that can contain spaces; the quotation marks keep that path together.

Get-Location and pwd observe the current directory. Set-Location and cd change it. New-Item -ItemType Directory creates a folder. Test-Path checks whether one exists. Do not use git submodule add as a synonym for creating a regular folder: it registers a separate Git repository and needs more careful review.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Working directory Folder used to interpret relative paths.
Absolute path Path that specifies its location independently of the working directory.
Relative path Path interpreted starting from the working directory.
Home directory Private starting folder associated with the signed-in account.
Parent directory Directory containing the current directory.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Create a practice folder within your own home

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$HOME\UmicomLearning" -Force

Expected observation: PowerShell shows the directory or confirms it exists.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Enter the directory

Set-Location "$HOME\UmicomLearning"

Expected observation: The prompt changes to your new working directory.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Confirm your location

Get-Location

Expected observation: The path ends in UmicomLearning.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Create a Notes subfolder

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path ".\Notes" -Force

Expected observation: You now have a Notes subfolder; no Umicom repository was touched.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 5 — Show the folder contents

Get-ChildItem

Expected observation: The Notes directory appears.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Create the equivalent Linux practice directory

mkdir -p "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes"

Expected observation: The folder is created or already exists.

Linux step 2 — Show exactly where you are

cd "$HOME/UmicomLearning" && pwd

Expected observation: The printed path ends in UmicomLearning.

Worked support scenario

A student working in C:\umicom\Umicom-Applications accidentally runs a file-creation example intended for a throwaway practice folder. The command may alter a real project. The safer pattern is to check Get-Location before every unfamiliar operation and enter the private training directory.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Using mkdir when a directory is supposed to be a Git submodule Do not pre-create a submodule destination; Git manages that folder.
Assuming cd creates a folder Use New-Item or mkdir to create, and cd to enter.
Forgetting quotes around a path with spaces Write Set-Location "C:\My Training", not an unquoted multiword path.

Exercise: demonstrate understanding

  1. Write down the purpose of two commands from this chapter, in your own words.
  2. Run a read-only command and record only the information needed to answer its question.
  3. Explain which command would change the machine, if any, and why the chapter avoids it.
  4. Explain the difference between an observation, a conclusion and an unverified assumption.

Review questions

  1. What is $HOME?
  2. What is the safest first command when you are unsure where you are?
Show the suggested answers
  1. The current user’s home directory in PowerShell.
  2. Get-Location or pwd.

How this connects to Umicom

Use a personal sandbox for all practice. Open real Umicom repositories only when a specific chapter asks you to inspect them, and never mix tutorial files into production folders.

Chapter 06 · Foundation

Chapter 06 — Create, open and read text files without scripting

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Create a Markdown note, read its contents and recognise file extensions.

Why this matters

A text file stores characters. A Markdown document (.md) is plain text with conventions for headings, links and lists. A C source file (.c) is also text but is interpreted by a compiler rather than a documentation renderer. A word-processing document (.docx) uses a different structured format. System administrators frequently inspect configuration and log files, so distinguishing these formats matters.

In the practice folder, use Notepad to create a short README.md. You do not need to write a PowerShell script to make this file. You can also write a short line interactively using Set-Content. However, the course does not create .ps1 or Python implementation files.

PowerShell Get-Content displays a text file. Get-Item reports file metadata such as size and modification time. Get-FileHash calculates a fingerprint used later when learning backup verification. Opening a text document is normally a reversible, low-risk activity, but opening an unknown executable or script is not equivalent.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Text editor Tool for changing plain-text files.
Extension Suffix such as .md, .txt or .c that often indicates format.
Metadata Information about a file, such as size and last modification time.
Encoding Rule for representing characters as bytes.
Markdown Readable plain-text formatting used by Bits2Banking lessons.

Worked support scenario

A Umicom learning contributor receives a request to fix an inaccurate documentation title. The correct tool is a text editor, not the C compiler. They read the file, change the smallest necessary phrase and verify the saved contents before considering a Git commit.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Writing text into the wrong directory Check Get-Location, then use the full expected file path.
Confusing opening a file with executing it Get-Content reads text; & .\program.exe executes a program.
Changing file extensions merely to make a file open Extensions do not convert the underlying format.

Chapter 07 · Foundation

Chapter 07 — Copy, rename and remove files carefully

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Distinguish reversible inspection from potentially destructive file operations.

Why this matters

Moving and deleting files are common administration tasks and common sources of mistakes. A copy creates another file while leaving the source intact. A move changes its location. A rename changes its name. A delete removes it from the location you select, and its recoverability depends on the method and system configuration.

PowerShell includes -WhatIf on many commands that change state. It displays the proposed action without executing it. This is useful when learning Remove-Item, Move-Item and Copy-Item. A preview is still not a substitute for checking the target path, but it can catch obvious surprises.

Always practise in $HOME\UmicomLearning; never experiment with C:\Windows, an installed program directory or a live Umicom repository. If you later administer shared servers, agree on the recovery and approval process before removing even a seemingly unimportant log or cache.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Copy Create a second file from existing content.
Move Relocate a file from one path to another.
Rename Change the file name without changing its contents.
WhatIf Request supported PowerShell commands to describe a change without making it.
Rollback Return a system to a known previous state after an unwanted change.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Return to the sandbox

Set-Location "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes"

Expected observation: You are working only in the practice Notes folder.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Preview a copy operation

Copy-Item .\README.md .\README-backup.md -WhatIf

Expected observation: PowerShell describes the copy but does not create the destination.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Create the practice backup

Copy-Item .\README.md .\README-backup.md

Expected observation: Two files now exist.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Preview a rename

Rename-Item .\README-backup.md -NewName "README-practice-copy.md" -WhatIf

Expected observation: The rename is shown, but not applied.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 5 — Preview a deletion and stop

Remove-Item .\README-practice-copy.md -WhatIf

Expected observation: The file remains present. We deliberately do not perform deletion in this exercise.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Copy within the sandbox

cp "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README.md" "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README-copy.md"

Expected observation: A second file exists; the original is unchanged.

Linux step 2 — Inspect both files

ls -l "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README"*

Expected observation: You see filenames and sizes before deciding on any cleanup.

Worked support scenario

An operator plans to clear space by deleting “old” reports. Before doing so, they identify the required retention period and whether a validated backup exists. They select a narrow set of files and preview the intended removal. This prevents a routine storage task from destroying audit evidence.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Using wildcard deletion without first listing matches Preview the exact matching files and avoid broad patterns.
Treating -Force as a fix for an unfamiliar error Understand why the action failed before overriding a check.
Believing a copy is a verified backup Read and compare the copied file; later chapters introduce fingerprints.

  2. It may remove work that has not been committed or backed up.

How this connects to Umicom

Umicom source preservation is mandatory. Refactoring does not authorise deleting previous functions, comments, educational explanations or features. Review and retain superseded code until the project owner approves removal.

Chapter 08 · Foundation

Chapter 08 — Install and verify PowerShell 7, Git and development tools

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Use trusted package managers and check that programs really work.

Why this matters

A package manager installs software from configured sources. On Windows, winget is the Windows Package Manager command-line interface. It is useful for installing PowerShell 7, Git, GitHub CLI and Visual Studio Code. You can run it from Windows PowerShell 5.1 while installing the newer PowerShell 7. The two products can coexist.

Before installing anything, run winget --version. If it is missing, consult Microsoft’s App Installer guidance rather than downloading an unfamiliar installer. When winget install is used, the package ID identifies the intended product. Review prompts about source agreements, licensing or elevated permissions rather than automatically accepting everything.

After installation, open a fresh terminal. Executable search paths may not refresh in an already-open shell. Get-Command tells you which executable the shell would run. A version command confirms that the program launches, which is different from proving it is compatible with a particular project build.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Package manager Software that installs and updates programs from configured sources.
Package ID Unique identifier, such as Git.Git, used to choose a package.
PATH Locations searched when you type an executable name.
CLI Command-line interface, such as gh for GitHub.
Toolchain Programs such as a compiler, CMake and Ninja used to build software.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Check that winget exists

winget --version

Expected observation: A version appears; if the command is not found, consult Microsoft installation guidance.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Inspect the PowerShell package before installing

winget show --id Microsoft.PowerShell --exact

Expected observation: Read the package name, publisher and installer information.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Install PowerShell 7 if needed

winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --exact --source winget

Expected observation: After any prompts and completion, open a new PowerShell 7 window.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Install Git when required

winget install --id Git.Git --exact --source winget

Expected observation: Git is installed; close and reopen the terminal to refresh PATH.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 5 — Install GitHub CLI when required

winget install --id GitHub.cli --exact --source winget

Expected observation: The gh command becomes available after installation.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 6 — Check which executables were installed

Get-Command pwsh, git, gh -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, Source

Expected observation: Available tools are listed with their installed paths.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Read package manager version on Ubuntu or Debian

apt --version

Expected observation: The package-manager version is displayed.

Linux step 2 — Inspect a package before requesting installation

apt show git

Expected observation: Package metadata appears when the distribution can find Git.

Worked support scenario

A beginner says “Git is installed but PowerShell cannot find it.” Instead of reinstalling repeatedly, ask them to close the old terminal, open a new PowerShell 7 window, run Get-Command git and then git --version. This distinguishes a PATH refresh issue from an actual installation failure.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Typing winget - -version The correct syntax is winget --version with adjacent hyphens.
Installing an unknown similarly named package Use the exact verified package ID and inspect winget show.
Believing successful installation proves authentication gh --version tests the program; gh auth status tests the GitHub sign-in.

  1. Why check Get-Command after installing a tool?
  2. Does winget install require you to write a PowerShell script?
Show the suggested answers
  1. It shows whether the shell can locate the intended executable.
  2. No. It is an interactive command; we do not add .ps1 implementation files.

How this connects to Umicom

For native C23 development, verify MSYS2 UCRT64 GCC, CMake and Ninja using the project’s documented toolchain. Do not mix toolchain families silently or change live build presets without reviewing them.

Chapter 09 · Foundation

Chapter 09 — Users, administrators and the meaning of permissions

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Explain which account runs a command and why elevated rights are exceptional.

Why this matters

Operating systems use identities to decide who may open, modify or execute a resource. Your signed-in account usually has a personal home folder and limited access to system-wide settings. An administrator account can perform more powerful operations. That extra power is useful for approved maintenance, but it also increases the damage a mistaken command can cause.

A permission is a rule attached to a resource. On Windows, NTFS access control lists can grant different rights to users and groups. On Linux, files have owners, groups and permission bits, with additional mechanisms such as ACLs. Changing permissions without understanding them can expose confidential documents or stop applications from working.

In this chapter we observe identity rather than changing membership or granting rights. If an installation asks for elevation, confirm that the source is trustworthy and that the installation is intended. Never solve a confusing error by turning off protection, recursively changing folder ownership or making the entire system writable.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Identity The user or service account under which an operation runs.
Administrator Account with elevated system-management privileges.
ACL Access control list specifying who may use a resource.
Group Set of accounts that may share permissions.
Permission denied Operating-system refusal because the account lacks required access.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Show the current identity

whoami

Expected observation: The Windows account name appears.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Display current identity and group context

whoami /groups

Expected observation: Group membership information is displayed.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Inspect permissions on a practice file

Get-Acl "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md" | Format-List Owner, AccessToString

Expected observation: The file owner and readable access rules are shown.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Verify your practice file exists before inspecting it

Test-Path "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md"

Expected observation: True indicates the file exists; False means you should complete Chapter 6.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Show the current user and groups

id

Expected observation: User ID, primary group and supplementary groups appear.

Linux step 2 — Inspect file permissions

ls -l "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README.md"

Expected observation: The permission string, owner and group appear if the file exists.

Worked support scenario

A colleague cannot edit a training document in a shared folder. First check which identity they are using and who owns the file. Do not immediately grant Everyone full control: establish what access the colleague actually needs and ask the resource owner to approve that permission.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Launching every terminal “as Administrator” Use a standard terminal unless a justified action requires elevation.
Applying recursive permission changes to unknown directories Inspect the relevant file and authorisation boundary first.
Confusing “file exists” with “I can write it” Existence and access permissions are separate checks.

Chapter 10 · Foundation

Chapter 10 — Processes: what is running on your computer?

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

List processes, read their resource use and avoid interrupting unknown work.

Why this matters

A process is a running instance of a program. The same application may create several processes, and different processes can share a program name. A process has an identifier, memory and access to resources. When an application appears frozen, inspecting its process and resource use can help establish whether it exists, is consuming CPU, or has exited unexpectedly.

Process names are not proof of trust. An unfamiliar process should be investigated using location, digital signature where available and the associated application rather than terminated immediately. Some background processes are critical to system operation. Stop-Process can end a process, potentially losing unsaved work; it is outside this beginner exercise.

The Windows Task Manager provides a graphical view of processes. PowerShell Get-Process gives a more inspectable textual form. Learning both helps when supporting people who prefer either a graphical interface or a command line.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Process Running instance of executable code.
PID Process identifier assigned by the operating system.
CPU Processor time used to execute work.
Working set Approximate physical memory currently held by a Windows process.
Task Manager Windows application for inspecting running processes and resources.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Show five processes

Get-Process | Select-Object -First 5 Name, Id, CPU

Expected observation: A short list appears; CPU values may be blank for some processes.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Sort processes by physical memory use

Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet64 -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 Name, Id, WorkingSet64

Expected observation: Processes with the largest reported working sets appear first.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Open Task Manager using the user interface

taskmgr

Expected observation: The Task Manager window opens; you may close it without changing anything.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — List processes from the terminal

ps -eo pid,comm,%cpu,%mem | head -n 10

Expected observation: A small process list appears.

Linux step 2 — Show system load averages

uptime

Expected observation: Linux displays uptime and load averages, if the utility is installed.

Worked support scenario

Umicom Studio reports a stalled build. You find that the compiler is still running and consuming CPU. That observation suggests ongoing compilation, not necessarily a crash. Next you inspect the build log and elapsed time. Terminating the compiler is a separate operational choice that should not be made simply because the UI looks idle.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Stopping the first process with a familiar name Verify PID, executable and ownership before considering termination.
Assuming high CPU usage always means failure Busy compilation and media encoding legitimately use CPU.
Treating the PID as permanent PIDs can be reused after a process exits.

Chapter 11 · Foundation

Chapter 11 — Windows services: background programs and startup

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Identify a Windows service and understand status without changing it.

Why this matters

Some programs begin running when the computer starts or when a user signs in. Windows services are a particular class of background programs managed through the Service Control Manager. A service can be running, stopped or in a transition. Not every background process is a Windows service, and not every stopped service indicates a fault: many start only when their feature is needed.

PowerShell Get-Service observes service status. Windows also provides the Services management console for a graphical view. Configuration and restart actions can affect other applications or users, so we do not run Restart-Service in this beginner chapter.

A reliable diagnostic identifies a particular service by name, records its state, consults the relevant events and verifies the user-visible function. An administrator should distinguish the technical process from the service the user actually cares about.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Windows service Background service managed by the Windows Service Control Manager.
Status Current observed service state, such as Running or Stopped.
Startup type Policy controlling when a service may start.
Dependency Another service required by a component.
Service manager Windows component that controls service lifecycle.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — List a few services

Get-Service | Select-Object -First 10 Name, DisplayName, Status

Expected observation: A short list of services is displayed.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Inspect details of a service that is installed

Get-Service -Name Spooler -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Format-List *

Expected observation: If the Print Spooler exists, PowerShell shows its properties; an empty result is not an error.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Open the graphical Services console

services.msc

Expected observation: A service list opens; view settings without modifying them.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Show services on a systemd-based Linux machine

systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager | head -n 12

Expected observation: A list of running systemd services appears where systemd is present.

Linux step 2 — Inspect a named service when installed

systemctl status ssh --no-pager

Expected observation: Status appears if the ssh unit exists; some distributions use sshd, and others may not have SSH installed.

Worked support scenario

A shared classroom printer is unavailable. The service name Spooler is relevant on Windows, but a stopped service alone does not prove the printer hardware or network is working. Record the service status, printer connection and reported queue state before choosing a fix.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Restarting an unknown service just to “see what happens” Observe its purpose and potential dependencies first.
Assuming every stopped service is broken Some services are optional or start only when needed.
Confusing startup applications with services Startup apps and service units use different management mechanisms.

Chapter 12 · Foundation

Chapter 12 — Windows Event Viewer and useful troubleshooting records

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Read event records safely and distinguish a symptom from its cause.

Why this matters

Programs, services and the operating system produce diagnostic events. A log record may include a timestamp, source and message. In Windows, Event Viewer groups records into logs such as Application and System. An Error event is worth investigating, but it does not automatically explain every user complaint, nor does the presence of warnings necessarily mean that a machine is unhealthy.

A useful investigation begins with the approximate time the problem occurred. Record the clock, including time zone if supporting someone remotely, then inspect the nearest relevant event and compare it with the user’s symptom. Use a small result limit so beginners are not overwhelmed by thousands of entries.

Some security logs require special privileges; do not request broader access simply to practise. Never delete event logs to make a warning disappear. Their value lies in retaining a trace of what happened.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Event log Structured history of diagnostic events.
Event ID Identifier for the event type, interpreted with its provider.
Provider Component that recorded the event.
Timestamp Recorded date and time.
Correlation Connecting events that belong to the same underlying incident.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — List details about the System log

Get-WinEvent -ListLog System | Select-Object LogName, RecordCount, IsEnabled

Expected observation: Windows reports log metadata if available.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Read five recent system events

Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 5 | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, ProviderName, LevelDisplayName

Expected observation: A short set of events appears.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Open Event Viewer

eventvwr.msc

Expected observation: A graphical console opens. Do not clear logs.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — View recent journal events if permitted

journalctl -n 10 --no-pager

Expected observation: Recent records appear; some systems restrict access by group membership.

Linux step 2 — Inspect only the current user journal where supported

journalctl --user -n 10 --no-pager

Expected observation: User-specific records appear if journal access is configured.

Worked support scenario

After an update, a reporting app fails to start. You record the failure time and compare the nearest related application event with the actual error displayed on screen. If the log refers to a missing DLL, you investigate package deployment before changing database records.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Searching the entire event history without a time range Start near the incident time and widen gradually.
Treating any warning as the root cause Check relevance, sequence and user impact.
Clearing logs to make a dashboard green Preserve evidence; clearing removes useful history.

How this connects to Umicom

Studio Problems, build logs, service health, and OS event records are separate evidence streams. Combine them without hiding errors or dropping the original transcript.

Chapter 13 · Foundation

Chapter 13 — Inspect processor, memory, Windows version and resources

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Gather a reproducible system profile without installing diagnosis software.

Why this matters

When a program runs slowly or fails to install, support teams often need the operating-system version, CPU architecture, available memory and free storage. These facts help identify compatibility problems and resource pressure. They are not performance guarantees. A machine with many CPU cores can still be limited by disk speed, memory pressure or a program waiting for network data.

PowerShell can query Windows management information using Get-CimInstance. The Win32_Processor class describes processors and core counts. Win32_ComputerSystem provides total physical memory. We display sizes in GiB-style binary units using the PowerShell 1GB numeric multiplier, and round the result for readability. The rounded value is an observation, not an inventory record of installed module part numbers.

In a shared support request, collect only the information needed to investigate the problem. Avoid publishing machine serial numbers, IP addresses or personal account paths in public issue reports unless explicitly approved.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Architecture Processor/OS instruction and binary compatibility family, such as x64.
Core Independent CPU execution unit.
Logical processor Thread execution context reported by the OS.
Capacity Resource amount, not necessarily current available resource.
GiB Binary unit equal to 1,073,741,824 bytes.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Read Windows release and architecture

Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object WindowsProductName, OsVersion, OsArchitecture

Expected observation: Windows release fields appear.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Read processor details

Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object Name, NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessors

Expected observation: CPU model and core/thread counts appear.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Read installed physical memory

[math]::Round((Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).TotalPhysicalMemory / 1GB, 2)

Expected observation: A rounded numeric value in binary gigabyte units appears.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Inspect available drive capacity

Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem

Expected observation: Drive capacities and free-space values appear for accessible file-system drives.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Show architecture

uname -m

Expected observation: The current machine architecture is printed.

Linux step 2 — Show memory

free -h

Expected observation: Used, available and total memory are displayed.

Linux step 3 — Show processor summary if utility exists

lscpu | head -n 15

Expected observation: CPU information appears when lscpu is installed.

Worked support scenario

A student cannot build a large native project on a low-memory laptop. Instead of assuming the compiler is defective, compare memory capacity, concurrent build jobs and log evidence. Reducing build parallelism from eight to two is a configuration decision, but first verify the actual machine constraints.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Confusing total and available memory Total memory is installed capacity; available is the amount the OS estimates can be used.
Publishing private device identifiers in a public issue Share only required, non-sensitive details.
Assuming a version string guarantees a toolchain works Run an actual configure/build/test acceptance for the intended project.

Chapter 14 · Foundation

Chapter 14 — Disks, backups and checking that restoration works

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Make and verify a training-file backup before learning recovery.

Why this matters

A disk stores information while the computer is switched off. A filesystem organises named files and directories on a storage volume. Different storage devices may expose more than one volume; the letter C: is a Windows convention, not a guarantee about the underlying physical device. Before changing storage configuration, determine whether a volume contains operating-system, program, user or recovery files.

A backup is useful only if you can recover a known version when needed. Simply copying a file is a first step; you should verify that the copy is readable and identical to the source. Hashes produce a compact fingerprint of file content. If two SHA-256 hashes differ, the files differ. Matching hashes provide very strong evidence of the same bytes, though a single copy in the same folder does not protect against disk failure, theft or ransomware.

This chapter uses only a small Markdown file in your practice directory. It does not partition, format, encrypt or erase any disk. Real organisational backups should include retention policy, separate storage, access controls and periodic restore tests.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Volume Logical storage area made available to the operating system.
Filesystem Data structure for organising files and directories.
Backup Recoverable copy kept according to an agreed policy.
Restore test Proof that data can be read from the backup.
SHA-256 Hash function commonly used to fingerprint file content.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Inspect accessible drives

Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem

Expected observation: The output lists drives and free space.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Return to your practice folder

Set-Location "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes"

Expected observation: Your README.md is the only file we will copy.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Make an extra copy

Copy-Item .\README.md .\README-verified-copy.md

Expected observation: The copy exists next to the original.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Get the original fingerprint

Get-FileHash .\README.md -Algorithm SHA256

Expected observation: A hexadecimal hash appears.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 5 — Get the copied fingerprint

Get-FileHash .\README-verified-copy.md -Algorithm SHA256

Expected observation: The hash should match the original exactly.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 6 — Read the restored copy

Get-Content .\README-verified-copy.md

Expected observation: You can read the content, demonstrating a small restore check.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Show available filesystem space

df -h

Expected observation: $HOME is normally stored on one of the listed filesystems.

Linux step 2 — Copy and verify a safe sample

cp "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README.md" "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README-verified-copy.md" && sha256sum "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README"*.md

Expected observation: The original and copied file should display matching hashes.

Worked support scenario

A charity office keeps important financial spreadsheets. A working local copy protects against an accidental edit, but not against a stolen computer. An appropriate real backup arrangement needs separate protected storage and a practice restoration, with personal information handled under the organisation’s policy.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Equating copies on one disk with disaster recovery Keep important backups on separate managed storage.
Backing up a file but never reopening it Verify readability and content after copying.
Running partition or format commands as practice Use read-only commands; destructive storage operations require separate authorised training.

  1. What does a mismatched SHA-256 hash tell you?
  2. Why is a copy next to the original not sufficient disaster protection?
Show the suggested answers
  1. The compared files do not have identical content.
  2. Both can be lost to the same disk failure or attack.

How this connects to Umicom

Before changing a repository, preserve source through Git commits and separately back up irreplaceable data. Git history is not a substitute for system backups or secret-management policy.

Chapter 15 · Foundation

Chapter 15 — IP addresses, networks, DNS and ports

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Identify the layers involved when a computer connects to a website or service.

Why this matters

A network connects devices that exchange messages. An IP address identifies a network interface in the relevant routing context. A router forwards traffic between networks. DNS maps names such as github.com to addresses. A TCP port identifies a service endpoint, such as port 443 commonly used for HTTPS. An HTTP application works above these layers.

A browser opening a GitHub page may depend on Wi-Fi or Ethernet, a valid IP configuration, working DNS, routing, a reachable server and TLS certificate validation. A failure at one layer can resemble a failure at another. For example, being able to reach a numeric IP does not prove name resolution works, while a failed ping does not prove HTTPS is broken because ICMP may be blocked.

Diagnostics should favour observation and approved destinations. This chapter uses public documentation domains as examples but does not imply that they are always reachable from every network. Avoid scanning arbitrary hosts or internal services unless you have permission.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
IP address Network-layer address used to deliver packets.
DNS System that resolves names to network addresses.
Router Device or service that forwards packets between networks.
TCP port Number identifying a transport endpoint on a host.
HTTPS HTTP carried over a secure TLS connection.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Review local IP configuration

Get-NetIPConfiguration

Expected observation: Windows reports interface address, gateway and DNS information where available.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Resolve a known host name

Resolve-DnsName github.com

Expected observation: A set of DNS records is returned when name resolution works.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Test an HTTPS service connection

Test-NetConnection github.com -Port 443

Expected observation: A TCP connection test result appears; firewall and network policy can affect it.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Inspect connection status without changing it

Get-NetAdapter | Select-Object Name, Status, LinkSpeed

Expected observation: Adapter status and reported link speed appear where supported.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Show local interfaces if ip is installed

ip -brief address

Expected observation: Addresses associated with interfaces appear.

Linux step 2 — Ask the resolver for GitHub

Expected observation: The resolver returns addresses when resolution succeeds.

Linux step 3 — Inspect routing entries

ip route

Expected observation: Linux displays configured routes.

Worked support scenario

A new contributor can open the terminal but cannot git clone from GitHub. You check whether they can resolve github.com and establish a TLS connection to the service. You then distinguish a connectivity failure from an authentication failure such as “repository not found” or “permission denied.”

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Assuming DNS is the same as the internet connection DNS resolves names; network routing and service access are separate.
Treating a failed ping as proof a website is down ICMP may be filtered; test the service port and protocol.
Publishing private network details publicly Mask sensitive addresses and network identifiers in support tickets.

Umicom Trader or Bank network adapters should use Framework-owned secure connectivity contracts. Beginners first learn to diagnose connections without implementing a new socket stack.
