Chapter 16 · Foundation

Chapter 16 — Troubleshoot a failed connection one layer at a time

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Record evidence distinguishing name resolution, connectivity and authentication problems.

Why this matters

A useful network investigation follows a sequence. First, identify the exact operation that failed and its error message. Second, check whether the local network interface is connected and has an address. Third, ask DNS for the remote name. Fourth, attempt a connection to the expected service port. Finally, inspect application authentication and permissions. Do not disable the firewall or certificate checks simply to see whether the problem disappears.

The order matters because some errors have unrelated causes. A GitHub push rejection saying “non-fast-forward” is not a network outage—it means the remote branch has history that your local push would not preserve. A TLS certificate warning is also different from failure to resolve a DNS name.

The commands in this chapter are read-only connection probes to a known public service. They may time out on restricted networks. Write down the outputs and tell the reader what conclusion is justified by each, rather than assuming success everywhere.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Connectivity Ability to exchange traffic with a service.
Timeout Operation failed to complete within a limit.
Firewall Policy enforcing which network traffic is allowed.
TLS Protocol protecting communication with authentication and encryption.
Authentication Process by which a system verifies account identity.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Check local adapter configuration

Get-NetIPConfiguration

Expected observation: An active interface normally has a valid address and gateway.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Test name resolution separately

Resolve-DnsName github.com

Expected observation: Addresses appear if the resolver succeeds.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Test the expected TCP endpoint

Test-NetConnection github.com -Port 443

Expected observation: A successful TCP test is separate evidence from a DNS lookup.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Check GitHub CLI authentication separately

gh auth status

Expected observation: The output describes account authentication if gh is installed.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Expected observation: An address result means the configured resolver returned a response.

Linux step 2 — Inspect service response headers with curl

Expected observation: An HTTP response or a specific TLS/network error appears; internet access is required.

Worked support scenario

Three contributors report “Git is broken.” One has no DNS response, one can reach GitHub but is not authenticated, and one has a non-fast-forward push rejection. They have different problems. A reproducible evidence sequence prevents installing software or editing repositories unnecessarily.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Disabling firewall protections to bypass a diagnostic Obtain authorisation and find the actual failing boundary instead.
Confusing authentication errors with routing errors Check reachability and gh auth status independently.
Assuming one successful request proves permanent reliability Repeat during the incident window and collect relevant logs.

Chapter 17 · Foundation

Chapter 17 — Linux terminal, home directory, files and processes

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Translate familiar Windows tasks into safe Linux equivalents.

Why this matters

Linux distributions usually provide a terminal emulator that starts a shell such as Bash. The user’s home directory is commonly under /home/username and is referred to as $HOME. Linux paths use / rather than Windows backslashes. pwd prints the current directory, ls lists entries, cd changes directory, and mkdir -p creates a directory tree.

A beginner does not need to memorise every shell option. They need to understand which system a command belongs to, how to request help and how to verify the result. PowerShell’s Get-ChildItem is conceptually similar to ls on Linux, although the programs differ in output and behaviour.

Linux commands can operate with elevated privileges through tools such as sudo. We avoid sudo in the initial exercises. A learner should know what a command is going to do before running it as an administrator.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Distribution Linux operating-system distribution with packaged software and configuration.
Bash Popular command shell on Linux.
Home directory Per-user location for personal data and settings.
sudo Command used to request privileged execution when authorised.
Process ID Operating-system identifier for a running process.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Expected observation: You see a subset of items in your Windows home.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

A student follows a Windows guide on a Linux laptop and tries Get-CimInstance, receiving “command not found.” They should not install unrelated packages at random. Instead, identify the intended information and use the Linux command (uname, free, df, ps) documented for that subject.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Using backslashes as Linux directory separators Linux commonly uses /.

Chapter 18 · Foundation

Chapter 18 — Linux permissions, packages, services and logs

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Observe essential Linux administration concepts without changing a shared system.

Why this matters

Linux often represents traditional file permissions with owner, group and mode bits. For a file, the r permission means read, w means write and x can mean execute. A directory has related but different access semantics: entering it requires search/execute permission. Permission output is a first clue, not a complete security model; ACLs and other mechanisms may also apply.

Package managers differ among distributions. Debian and Ubuntu commonly use apt; Fedora often uses dnf; Arch Linux uses pacman. There is no universal command that you should copy from one distribution to another. We keep the exercises observational: inspect packages and service status, but do not start automatic upgrades without approval.

Systemd is common on Linux machines and uses services called units, but other init systems exist. Logs may be in the systemd journal or files under /var/log. The current account’s permissions determine what can be read.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Owner/group Account and group associated with a file.
Mode bits Traditional rwx permissions shown by ls -l.
apt Package-manager interface on Debian-derived systems.
systemd unit Configuration and state of a managed Linux service.
journalctl Command for reading systemd journal events.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — From PowerShell inspect a practice Windows file as comparison

Get-Item "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md" | Select-Object Name, Length

Expected observation: You see Windows file metadata; Linux commands below are separate.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Expected observation: UID, GID and groups are printed.

Expected observation: Recent journal events appear or permissions restrict access.

Worked support scenario

A Linux service stops after an upgrade. First check the unit state and relevant journal messages, then identify the exact package version and configuration changes. Do not run a broad upgrade or reset permissions simply because one service failed.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Treating chmod 777 as a normal troubleshooting tool It grants overly broad access; understand the correct policy first.
Running apt upgrade automatically as a practice task Inspect updates and obtain permission before changing installed software.
Assuming journal entries are visible to every user Log access can be restricted by account and group.

Umicom OS host and recovery services should be diagnosed at the correct privilege boundary. Learners should distinguish a Linux service problem from a bug in Umicom Framework user-space code.

Chapter 19 · Foundation

Chapter 19 — Git from zero: create, inspect, stage and commit

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Make a complete history of a practice document before publishing anything.

Why this matters

Git keeps versions of project files locally. A working tree is the files you are editing. The staging area selects changes for the next commit. A commit records a snapshot with an identifier, an author and an explanation. A branch is a movable reference to a line of commits; main is commonly the default branch. Git works without GitHub, which is a remote hosting service.

You can learn Git safely in a private practice folder without a remote. This prevents experimental commits from entering real Umicom repositories. Keep changes small and messages specific. Inspect git diff before staging and git diff --cached after staging. git add -A includes deletions as well as additions; reviewing is essential.

For the first exercise create a repository under $HOME\UmicomLearning\git-first-project. Do not call git init inside an existing parent Git repository unless that nesting is intentional. The practice area is separate from the actual Umicom-Applications workspace.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Working tree Editable files visible on disk.
Index/staging area Selected snapshot waiting for the next commit.
Commit Identified, recorded version of a repository.
Branch Named reference to a commit history.
Remote Another Git repository address, often on GitHub.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Create a dedicated Git practice folder

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$HOME\UmicomLearning\git-first-project" -Force

Expected observation: The folder exists without affecting existing Umicom repositories.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Enter the folder and begin Git history

Set-Location "$HOME\UmicomLearning\git-first-project"
git init -b main

Expected observation: Git reports it created an empty repository on main.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Write an introductory Markdown file

Expected observation: README.md now contains a short heading.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Inspect unstaged changes

git status
git diff -- README.md

Expected observation: Status reports README.md as untracked; an untracked file does not appear in ordinary git diff.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 5 — Stage the file and review the snapshot

git add -A
git diff --cached --check
git diff --cached

Expected observation: The staged diff contains the README addition; no unrelated file should appear.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 6 — Commit the reviewed file

git commit -m "docs: start practice project"

Expected observation: Git records one local commit.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 7 — Inspect the history

git log --oneline -3
git status

Expected observation: One commit appears; status should report a clean working tree.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Use Git in an independent Linux practice folder

mkdir -p "$HOME/UmicomLearning/git-first-project" && cd "$HOME/UmicomLearning/git-first-project" && git init -b main

Expected observation: An empty practice repository is created. Configure author identity before committing.

Worked support scenario

A contributor is editing two files: an approved documentation correction and an unrelated experimental configuration change. Before git add -A, they inspect both changes. If they are unrelated, they stage only the approved document. The ability to control the snapshot is why Git has a staging area.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Confusing git add with publishing git add stages locally; git push publishes commits to a remote.
Committing from the wrong directory Verify Get-Location and git status before staging.
Assuming untracked files appear in git diff Use git status and stage a file before viewing its staged diff.

Chapter 20 · Foundation

Chapter 20 — GitHub: authenticate, publish and collaborate responsibly

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Understand the difference between a local commit and an online repository.

Why this matters

GitHub hosts Git repositories and adds collaboration features such as issues, reviews and pull requests. GitHub CLI is an optional command-line program named gh that can manage repositories and authentication from PowerShell. git records and synchronises commits; gh interacts with GitHub services. They are complementary, not interchangeable.

A Git user name and email identify commit authors; they are not credentials for accessing GitHub. Authentication is separate and should be performed through the supported sign-in process. gh auth status checks whether a user is signed in, and gh auth login starts an interactive flow. Never place access tokens or passwords inside a repository.

A beginner should publish a private practice repository first. Public repositories are useful for open-source collaboration but can expose accidentally committed data. Review the complete staged snapshot and repository visibility before creating a remote. Creating a repository on an organisation account additionally requires permission; most beginners should use their own account.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
GitHub Online hosting and collaboration platform for Git repositories.
GitHub CLI Command-line interface (gh) for GitHub operations.
Authentication Proof that an account is authorised to access a service.
Private repository Repository visible only to granted accounts.
Pull request Proposed change submitted for review before integration.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

A new Umicom contributor cannot push to the Foundation repository because they do not have direct write permission. That is expected for many collaborators. They can contribute through a personal fork and pull request. Project maintainers with authorised access may use the project’s direct-to-main policy; permission boundaries still apply.

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Treating git config user.email as GitHub authentication Use gh auth login for sign-in.
Creating a public repository for private practice by accident Choose --private, inspect the destination and avoid secrets.
Re-running gh repo create when the remote already exists Inspect git remote -v and gh repo view before creating anything else.

Chapter 21 · Foundation

Chapter 21 — Create a new Umicom application: repositories, modules and discovery

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Understand the supplied Umicom project creation guide and its future-automation boundary.

Why this matters

The included document Creating a New Umicom Application — A Beginner’s PowerShell Guide and Automatic Registration Blueprint explains how an application may be split between a standalone parent repository and a reusable application-module repository. It uses a fictional Umicom Notes product, with Framework linked as a submodule and the same Notes module referenced from two parents. This is a useful architecture example, not an instruction to create live GitHub repositories during a classroom exercise.

A Git submodule points to an exact commit in another repository. Parent repositories can pin different commits even when both refer to the same remote module. This matters in Umicom Applications and Umicom OS: updating Framework code in one checkout does not automatically update every parent gitlink. Git registration also does not guarantee CMake build registration.

The supplied guide distinguishes currently documented manual CMake registration from a proposed future native, Framework-owned auto-discovery workflow. Do not treat its umicom project create ... --standalone ... --suite example as an existing command. The planned implementation must be reviewed, permissions verified, and tests passed before anyone may rely on it.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Standalone parent Repository that composes Framework and an application module.
Application module Reusable independently versioned product-specific source.
Submodule gitlink Parent reference to one commit of another repository.
Manifest Declared application identity, frontend and build metadata.
Auto-discovery blueprint Future plan, not evidence that the capability is implemented.

A healthcare contributor wants a new application module. They begin by identifying whether a module repository already exists, which parent application will compose it, which manifest the Framework understands, and whether the code can build with current CMake. They do not blindly paste three new CMake sections into a shared build configuration before reviewing the latest project capabilities.

Cloning Framework source into every module manually Reuse one authoritative Framework repository through pinned submodules.

Chapter 22 · Foundation

Chapter 22 — Build, test and inspect a read-only C23 program

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Use GCC, CMake and CTest to understand how native programs are built and verified.

Why this matters

A compiler translates C source into machine code. CMake describes build targets and configuration. Ninja executes build steps efficiently. CTest runs registered tests and reports their outcome. Each performs a different part of the workflow. A successful compilation is not the same as a passing test suite, and passing tests are not a claim of complete production readiness.

This update includes a small standalone laboratory under labs/native/sysadmin-readonly-text. Its native C23 program reads a text file, counts bytes and logical lines, and refuses binary or oversized inputs. It does not edit the file, scan privileged system paths or silently truncate content. The tests use checked-in fixtures and show success as well as deliberate rejection.

For a beginner, the purpose is twofold: see how the software tools fit together and understand that a read-only diagnostic program can still report errors responsibly. For the real Umicom project, shared production file services must remain Framework-owned rather than being duplicated from this educational sample.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Compiler Program that translates C23 source into executable machine code.
CMake Declarative build-configuration tool.
Ninja Native build execution engine.
CTest Test runner used by CMake projects.
Fail closed Reject invalid or incomplete input instead of pretending the result is valid.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

A student receives “CMake cannot find gcc”. They check gcc --version and Get-Command gcc, then confirm the UCRT64 compiler path. They do not change C23 code to solve a missing tool. After the toolchain is detected, a failed CTest case is investigated separately from compilation.

Chapter 23 · Foundation

Chapter 23 — Troubleshoot problems systematically and write useful evidence

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Apply a repeatable incident investigation without deleting evidence.

Why this matters

Troubleshooting starts with a precise symptom, not a speculative fix. Record what the user expected, what actually happened, the time, the computer and program versions, the smallest steps that reproduce it, and the exact error message. Next form a hypothesis and choose a low-risk test that could disprove it. Keep the raw evidence even after the issue is resolved.

One important distinction is between symptoms and causes. “The screen is blank” is a symptom. It might be caused by a closed application, a display driver, a file that failed to load or a network connection. A useful administrator narrows the possibilities layer by layer. Do not run broad cleanup commands, reinstall unrelated tools or disable security simply because an error message is unfamiliar.

For a learning community, communication is part of diagnosis. Another contributor should be able to repeat the exact steps and understand which tests were performed. Avoid including passwords, tokens, patients’ records, private file paths or complete network inventories in public issue reports.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Symptom Observed effect of a problem.
Hypothesis Proposed explanation that can be tested.
Reproduction Steps that cause the issue to happen again.
Evidence Saved output, logs or observations supporting an investigation.
Regression Previously working behaviour that fails after a change.

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Worked support scenario

A contributor reports a native Umicom test crash. Capture the failing test name, exact CTest output, compiler, target preset, Git SHA, whether a submodule differs from its parent pin, and whether the same test fails repeatedly. That evidence is far more valuable than “the build is broken.”

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Sending only a screenshot of the last error line Include the surrounding command, versions and preceding failure where relevant.
Changing several unrelated settings at once Apply one reviewed change, retest, and attribute the outcome correctly.
Pushing experimental fixes before tests pass Keep changes local until the required validation gates succeed.

Chapter 24 · Foundation

Chapter 24 — Capstone: perform a safe support check from start to finish

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation
Audience: first-time users and returning learners; no prior system-administration knowledge required.
Code policy: interactive PowerShell 7 and Bash commands; native C23/Assembly for Umicom executable development.
Estimated study time: 25–50 minutes (longer when practising).

What you will learn

Combine terminal use, system facts, a sample backup, Git and testing into one evidence-based exercise.

Why this matters

The capstone combines skills from the course without requiring administrator privileges or changing any live Umicom source. Imagine a friend says the learning Notes application will not save a document and Git reports confusing changes. Your job is to identify the computer, confirm the working directory, inspect the practice file, preserve a copy, review Git status if working in a repository, and produce a short factual report.

A complete answer distinguishes observed facts from assumptions. You might be able to show that the practice file exists, is readable and has a matching verified copy. That does not prove that the user’s separate Notes application works. Similarly, a clean Git working tree says nothing about whether the latest revision passes CTest.

This exercise is appropriate for individual learners, classrooms and supervised volunteer training. Do it inside your personal $HOME\UmicomLearning sandbox. Do not inspect other people’s files or actual charity beneficiary records.

New words, explained

Term Plain-English meaning
Checklist Ordered, verifiable sequence of administration actions.
Evidence bundle Collected outputs supporting what was checked.
Known limitation A test or observation that remains unverified.
Acceptance criterion Clear condition required to call a step successful.
Handover Record that allows another person to continue the investigation.

Windows practice — PowerShell 7

Before typing: Run these commands in a normal, non-elevated PowerShell window. Where a file is used, complete the previous practice-folder chapters first. Do not paste the PS C:\...> prompt into the terminal.

Start: Use the Windows Start menu or Windows Terminal to open PowerShell. Check the prompt is ready. Commands beginning with $ are still commands; type them exactly as shown.

Step 1 — Confirm your active shell and user

$PSVersionTable.PSVersion
whoami

Expected observation: Write down PowerShell version and account name.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 2 — Record OS and CPU context

Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object WindowsProductName, OsArchitecture
Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object -First 1 Name

Expected observation: A small environment inventory is displayed.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 3 — Confirm the exact practice file

Test-Path "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md"

Expected observation: True means the training document exists.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 4 — Read it, not execute it

Get-Content "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md"

Expected observation: The expected Markdown heading appears.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 5 — Verify backup and file identity

Get-FileHash "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md" -Algorithm SHA256
Get-FileHash "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README-verified-copy.md" -Algorithm SHA256

Expected observation: Hashes should match if Chapter 14 created the copy and it has not changed.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Step 6 — Inspect any practice Git status

Set-Location "$HOME\UmicomLearning\git-first-project"
git status

Expected observation: Git reports the current branch and modified/untracked files, if any.

Check: Read the output before continuing. If it does not match, stop and investigate the specific command; do not add -Force or run as Administrator automatically.

Linux comparison — terminal/Bash

Linux commands are alternatives on a Linux machine or authorised VM. Do not paste them into Windows PowerShell as though the shells have identical syntax.

Linux step 1 — Confirm location, user and free space

whoami && pwd && df -h "$HOME"

Expected observation: Read-only user and storage context is shown.

Linux step 2 — Verify safe backup if present

sha256sum "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README.md" "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README-verified-copy.md"

Expected observation: Matching hashes are expected if both copies are unchanged.

Worked support scenario

Write a five-sentence handover: “I checked the account and the OS, inspected the sandbox path, confirmed the Notes Markdown file can be read, verified its copied hash, and observed the practice Git repository status. I did not inspect the real user’s documents or alter system configuration. Further work is required to reproduce the reported application save failure.”

Common problems and how to respond

Problem or assumption Better response
Marking the whole incident resolved because one file is readable Distinguish sandbox evidence from the original user problem.
Ignoring warnings from missing files Record “not run” and return to the prerequisite chapter instead of inventing success.
Posting full log contents publicly Remove credentials and private identifiers before sharing.

Exercise: demonstrate understanding

  1. Write down the purpose of two commands from this chapter, in your own words.
  2. Run a read-only command and record only the information needed to answer its question.
  3. Explain which command would change the machine, if any, and why the chapter avoids it.
  4. Explain the difference between an observation, a conclusion and an unverified assumption.

Review questions

  1. What is an honest “not verified” outcome?
  2. Which actions in this capstone modify live Umicom code?
Show the suggested answers
  1. A statement that a required check could not be completed with available evidence.
  2. None. All exercises use observation and private practice files.

How this connects to Umicom

Capstone acceptance requires clear evidence and honest reporting, not a perfect-looking dashboard. The same practice applies to real Umicom Kernel boot tests, Studio CTest results, and Framework/OS gitlink qualification.

Where to go next

Return to the course contents and complete the final assessment before attempting advanced system changes.

Chapter 25 · Intermediate

Chapter 25 — Users, groups and why identity matters

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation

Audience: first-time users and returning learners; practical examples appropriate for supervised younger learners.

Estimated study time: 45–65 minutes.

Prerequisites: Chapters 2 and 9.

Why this matters

A volunteer signs in to a shared training computer and sees that they can read a sample document but cannot install software. Another user can install software but cannot view the volunteer’s private files. Both outcomes may be correct. System administration begins by understanding which account is acting and what that account is permitted to do, rather than trying to make every operation work by elevating privileges.

What you will be able to do

By the end of this chapter you should be able to explain the new terms in ordinary language, select a safe read-only command for the right operating system, recognise a normal result and identify an unverified result. You should also be able to describe what permission would be needed before making a real system change.

The mental model

A user account answers “who is doing this?”. A group answers “which collection of users shares a permission?”. Authentication proves identity; authorisation checks whether that identity can take an action. A signed-in person can also start programs that run with another identity, such as a Windows service account or a Linux daemon. Do not confuse the visible account name with the privileges of every process. Windows also has a distinction between being a member of Administrators and actually running an elevated process under User Account Control (UAC). Linux commonly separates an ordinary account from controlled administrator actions performed with sudo.

How accounts become effective permissions

Imagine an online classroom with a teacher, a learner and an application server. The learner must read lessons and create documents in their own folder. The teacher may edit shared lessons, and a background publishing service may read approved Markdown material. These are three distinct roles, not three reasons to make every account a local administrator. The right question is “which operation must this identity perform on which resource?”. Identify the smallest privilege that satisfies that task.

In a multi-user environment, membership can change while a session remains active. A permission update may not immediately affect an already issued access token or group membership visible to a running process. This is one reason an access problem should be reproduced with the same user and session rather than tested only as an administrator. A Windows computer joined to a domain may also display domain identity information unavailable to the local account commands used in this lesson. Record the environment rather than assuming all Windows computers are identical.

Words you should know

Term Meaning
Identity An account or principal whose actions can be attributed.
Group A set of accounts that may share permissions.
Privilege A permission with system-wide consequences.
Least privilege Giving an account only the authority needed for its work.
Service account An identity used by background software rather than everyday interactive use.

Windows: PowerShell 7, one command at a time

Use a normal non-elevated PowerShell window. Do not type the PS C:\...> prompt. If a command is unavailable or returns Access Denied, record that result; do not attempt to defeat the restriction.

The lines in a code block may contain more than one interactive command. Run them in order, checking each result before continuing. No .ps1 file is created or required.

Windows step 1 — Identify the signed-in account

whoami

Expected result: A computer or domain name followed by the account name. This is identity, not a list of all privileges.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 2 — Read the groups for this session

whoami /groups

Expected result: Group membership and attributes appear. Do not copy the complete output into public chat; it can identify your organisation.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 3 — Inspect local users without changing them

Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name, Enabled

Expected result: Local account names and enabled state on supported Windows editions. A domain-managed or restricted machine may return an error: record that limitation.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 4 — Check your shell identity explicitly

[System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name

Expected result: A text identifier for the Windows security context of this process.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Linux: terminal and distribution differences

Run the following only in an authorised Linux computer or VM. If you use Windows only, read this section for comparison. A program being absent does not mean the whole operating system is faulty.

Linux step 1 — Identify the running account

id

Expected result: User ID (UID), primary group ID (GID) and supplementary groups.

Linux step 2 — Show the short account name

whoami

Expected result: The effective user for the current command.

Linux step 3 — Inspect groups in a friendly format

groups

Expected result: Group names for the current user; membership is not a reason to alter groups.

Worked support scenario

A student cannot create a folder under C:\Program Files. Rather than reopening everything as Administrator, first inspect the current identity, then choose a personal learning directory such as $HOME\UmicomLearning. Installation into protected locations is a separate, explicitly authorised activity. If a service fails under its own account, the correct investigation concerns that service identity and the exact resource it needs—not the identity of the engineer who happens to be watching.

Common mistakes and safe responses

Mistake Better response
“I belong to Administrators, so every process is elevated.” UAC commonly starts ordinary processes with restricted privileges; membership and effective rights differ.
“Make the student administrator to fix it.” Check the intended folder and required action first; use a user-writable practice location.
“A service uses the currently signed-in account.” Many services run under independently configured identities.

Exercises

  1. Write down the difference between authentication and authorisation.

  2. Explain why inspecting groups is safer than adding everyone to a privileged group.

  3. Imagine a backup service cannot read a private directory. Identify two facts to collect before proposing any change.

Review questions and suggested answers

Show the suggested answers after attempting the exercises

  1. Authentication checks who you are; authorisation checks what that identity may do.

  2. Adding privilege affects many more resources and hides the actual root cause.

  3. Record the service identity and the intended directory ACL before any modification.

Production Umicom software should use the appropriate Umicom Framework service for identities, processes, filesystem operations, Git, diagnostics, build planning or observability. The teaching commands here are interactive; they are not substitute Python or PowerShell implementations. Any reusable new executable component must first be considered for Framework ownership and designed in C23 or justified Assembly.

  • https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/id-invocation.html

Chapter 26 · Intermediate

Chapter 26 — Understand file permissions without opening private data

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation

Audience: first-time users and returning learners; practical examples appropriate for supervised younger learners.

Estimated study time: 50–75 minutes.

Prerequisites: Chapter 25 and Chapter 7.

Why this matters

A project README is visible in one folder but access is denied in another. A beginner may assume the file has disappeared. Often the file exists, but the operating system has correctly refused an operation. The administrator’s job is to explain access decisions without bypassing the owner or exposing private files.

What you will be able to do

By the end of this chapter you should be able to explain the new terms in ordinary language, select a safe read-only command for the right operating system, recognise a normal result and identify an unverified result. You should also be able to describe what permission would be needed before making a real system change.

The mental model

A folder path tells you where an item is; permissions decide who may read, write, or traverse it. Windows NTFS uses access-control lists (ACLs) with entries applying to users and groups. Rights may be inherited from the containing folder, and an explicit deny entry can influence access. Linux traditionally shows owner, group and other read/write/execute bits; directories use execute for traversal, so being able to read the directory name list is not the same as reaching a file. Additional ACL mechanisms and security layers can apply on either system. Never conclude “everyone can read” from one superficial permission view.

What “effective access” really asks

Consider a Notes project with a docs directory. On Linux, a file may be readable according to its own mode but still inaccessible if the user lacks traverse permission on a parent directory. On Windows, an inherited ACL entry might grant read access while another relevant identity or policy changes the overall result. File ownership may permit altering permissions but does not automatically imply every ordinary access request succeeds. The exact behaviour depends on the operating system and the file and share permission layers involved.

Do not test private documents to discover access rights. Use a file you own. The responsible administrator asks the owner of the resource to approve any change and documents the intended access policy before modifying ACLs. The goal is not to make an error disappear; it is to ensure only the people and services with a genuine need can use the resource.

Words you should know

Term Meaning
ACL An access-control list of permissions and identities.
Inheritance A child receiving permission rules from its parent.
Read Permission to inspect content, when other controls allow it.
Write Permission to change content or metadata.
Traverse Permission to pass through a directory to reach a child.

Windows: PowerShell 7, one command at a time

Use a normal non-elevated PowerShell window. Do not type the PS C:\...> prompt. If a command is unavailable or returns Access Denied, record that result; do not attempt to defeat the restriction.

The lines in a code block may contain more than one interactive command. Run them in order, checking each result before continuing. No .ps1 file is created or required.

Windows step 1 — Confirm your own practice document exists

Test-Path "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md"

Expected result: True only if the training file exists at that path; if False, complete Chapter 6 or substitute your own harmless practice document.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 2 — Examine its owner and ACL

Get-Acl "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md" | Format-List Owner, Access

Expected result: Entries identify permissions and inheritance. The list may be extensive.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 3 — View an alternative built-in Windows ACL report

icacls "$HOME\UmicomLearning\Notes\README.md"

Expected result: Rights may appear as letter codes; this command only displays when called with no changes.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Linux: terminal and distribution differences

Run the following only in an authorised Linux computer or VM. If you use Windows only, read this section for comparison. A program being absent does not mean the whole operating system is faulty.

Linux step 1 — Inspect the permission string on your own test file

ls -l "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README.md"

Expected result: Owner, group, size and mode are shown.

Linux step 2 — Inspect mode numerically on GNU/Linux

stat -c "%a %U %G %n" "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes/README.md"

Expected result: Numerical mode, user, group and path. Other Unix variants use different stat options.

Linux step 3 — Inspect the directory separately

ls -ld "$HOME/UmicomLearning/Notes"

Expected result: Notice x on a directory permits traversal; it is not file execution.

Worked support scenario

A colleague says “please run chmod -R 777 because my Notes app cannot save”. Explain why the request is unsafe: it changes rights recursively, including files never involved in the incident, and grants broad access. Instead, identify the exact directory, the service identity, the operation attempted and any relevant OS or application log. Demonstrate by reading permissions on your own practice file, with no permission changes.

Common mistakes and safe responses

Mistake Better response
“Read-only commands should be run as Administrator just in case.” Normal-user inspection is the default; escalation should be justified, reviewed and time-limited.
“A Linux x bit always means running a program.” On directories, x means search/traverse permission.
“An ACL line fully explains every access decision.” Inheritance, groups and additional controls may influence the effective result.

Exercises

  1. Explain the three common Linux permission classes.

  2. Identify one reason a file might exist yet remain inaccessible.

  3. Find the owner of a harmless file you created for training, then stop without changing its ACL.

Review questions and suggested answers

Show the suggested answers after attempting the exercises

  1. Owner, group and other; an ACL can add further granularity.

  2. Insufficient permission on the file or a parent directory, among other possibilities.

  3. Use Get-Acl or ls -l; no elevation or broad permission changes are needed.

Chapter 27 · Intermediate

Chapter 27 — Investigate a Windows service and its event records

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation

Audience: first-time users and returning learners; practical examples appropriate for supervised younger learners.

Estimated study time: 45–70 minutes.

Prerequisites: Chapters 10–12.

Why this matters

An application window will not open. Restarting the entire computer might hide the problem temporarily, but it does not explain it. Windows has background services that support networking, software updates and many other functions. We will learn to inspect those services without stopping or reconfiguring them.

What you will be able to do

By the end of this chapter you should be able to explain the new terms in ordinary language, select a safe read-only command for the right operating system, recognise a normal result and identify an unverified result. You should also be able to describe what permission would be needed before making a real system change.

The mental model

A Windows service is a background program managed by the Service Control Manager. It has a configuration, an account, dependencies and a runtime status such as Running or Stopped. A process can exist while the service is unhealthy; a service can also be deliberately Stopped when not required. An event log records messages generated by Windows and applications. Look for a sequence: when was the last successful startup, what changed immediately before failure, and was the failure in the application, a dependency or access to a resource? Event timestamps are observations, not proof of causation.

Separate a service state from a user-visible outcome

A service manager reports lifecycle information: configured start type, process state and sometimes exit codes. A student needs to know whether an application can actually complete a task. These are different checks. A service can report Running while its database credentials are expired, its dependency is slow or its listener is on the wrong port. Likewise, a stopped Print Spooler is not evidence that a headless C23 test machine is faulty.

When reading events, limit the time range and choose a relevant provider if possible. A System log contains many unrelated messages. A useful support report records a specific user-visible failure at 10:12, then examines events immediately before and after 10:12 for the correct service. A timestamp without a matching process, machine and operation is context, not causation. Keep raw logs in an approved restricted location rather than pasting them into a public report.

Words you should know

Term Meaning
Service A background program managed by the operating system.
Dependency Another component required for correct operation.
Event ID An identifier issued by a log provider for a kind of event.
Provider The component that wrote a log record.
Incident timeline An ordered view of observations surrounding a problem.

Windows: PowerShell 7, one command at a time

Use a normal non-elevated PowerShell window. Do not type the PS C:\...> prompt. If a command is unavailable or returns Access Denied, record that result; do not attempt to defeat the restriction.

The lines in a code block may contain more than one interactive command. Run them in order, checking each result before continuing. No .ps1 file is created or required.

Windows step 1 — List a small sample of services

Get-Service | Select-Object -First 12 Name, Status, DisplayName

Expected result: Several services appear. Do not treat every Stopped service as broken.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 2 — Inspect a known service only when present

Get-Service -Name Spooler -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

Expected result: The Print Spooler may be absent or disabled; no output is a valid observation.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 3 — Read recent Application log events

Get-WinEvent -LogName Application -MaxEvents 8 | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, ProviderName, LevelDisplayName

Expected result: Recent entries are displayed. If access is refused, note that the log requires different authorisation.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 4 — Read service-related Windows records

Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = "System"; ProviderName = "Service Control Manager" } -MaxEvents 8 | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, Message

Expected result: Where events exist, compare their timestamps with the reported failure. Some messages contain identifying information; keep them private.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Linux: terminal and distribution differences

Run the following only in an authorised Linux computer or VM. If you use Windows only, read this section for comparison. A program being absent does not mean the whole operating system is faulty.

Linux step 1 — Compare the concept with running services on systemd hosts

systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager

Expected result: Service unit names appear if systemd is used.

Linux step 2 — Read recent system journal entries when allowed

journalctl -n 8 --no-pager

Expected result: Some records may be hidden from ordinary users; do not escalate automatically.

Worked support scenario

A training web-server exercise shows a connection refusal. You inspect the expected process, the port, and the relevant application log. If the service never started, the problem is not necessarily networking. If it started but binds the wrong interface, the service can be Running but still unusable to the intended client. Write down the exact reported status, time, and tested endpoint before suggesting a restart.

Common mistakes and safe responses

Mistake Better response
“Stopped always means failed.” Services can be manual, disabled or simply not needed at present.
“A successful Start command proves the application works.” Probe the actual dependent function; process existence is not end-to-end health.
“All Event ID numbers are globally unique.” Use the event provider plus ID and relevant timestamp when interpreting logs.

Exercises

  1. Find one service without changing its state; report only its name and status.

  2. Identify the extra facts needed to connect a log entry to an incident.

  3. Explain why you should not paste full logs containing paths, usernames or credentials into public chats.

Review questions and suggested answers

Show the suggested answers after attempting the exercises

  1. Get-Service is read-only; choose an ordinary service.

  2. Provider, time, event identifier, affected service and observed symptom.

  3. Logs may contain identifiable or confidential information; share only redacted excerpts.

Chapter 28 · Intermediate

Chapter 28 — Understand Linux systemd units, logs and safe inspection

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation

Audience: first-time users and returning learners; practical examples appropriate for supervised younger learners.

Estimated study time: 45–65 minutes.

Prerequisites: Chapters 17–18 and 27.

Why this matters

On a Linux host, the same application may run as a systemd service rather than a Windows service. A beginner can still ask the same useful questions: Which component should be running? What state is it in? Who started it? What evidence shows that the application works?

What you will be able to do

By the end of this chapter you should be able to explain the new terms in ordinary language, select a safe read-only command for the right operating system, recognise a normal result and identify an unverified result. You should also be able to describe what permission would be needed before making a real system change.

The mental model

Many Linux distributions use systemd as the system and service manager. A unit is a declarative description of a managed resource; service units commonly end in .service. System units and per-user units are different. The journalctl command reads the systemd journal, where records may be restricted by permissions and may not persist after restart on some configurations. A container or a Windows Subsystem for Linux environment may not be running systemd at all. Learning to recognise “not applicable” is more professional than issuing commands until something stops reporting an error.

Why user services are different from system services

A desktop user may run a background synchronisation process attached to their login session. A server may run the same kind of process as a system unit using a dedicated service account. These lifetimes and permission boundaries are different. A command using systemctl --user asks the user service manager; a command without --user usually asks the system manager. Neither should be used to modify a service merely because its name sounds familiar.

The presence of systemctl does not guarantee systemd is PID 1. Some containers, rescue environments and distributions use different service managers, and a limited systemd instance may not have all journal facilities. Start by reading the environment. If a service's unit and journal are unavailable, record the limitation and consult the local operating-system guidance rather than installing services or creating config files without permission.

Words you should know

Term Meaning
Unit A systemd configuration describing a managed resource.
Service unit A unit that manages a process or service.
User unit A systemd unit managed within a user session.
Journal A structured collection of messages managed by systemd-journald.
Enabled Configured to be activated by dependency/startup triggers; not the same as currently active.

Windows: PowerShell 7, one command at a time

Use a normal non-elevated PowerShell window. Do not type the PS C:\...> prompt. If a command is unavailable or returns Access Denied, record that result; do not attempt to defeat the restriction.

The lines in a code block may contain more than one interactive command. Run them in order, checking each result before continuing. No .ps1 file is created or required.

Windows step 1 — Compare the current system’s manager

Get-Service | Select-Object -First 5 Name, Status

Expected result: Windows uses Service Control Manager rather than systemd.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 2 — Open the documentation before changing anything

Get-Help Get-Service -Online

Expected result: Only opens an official help page if browser access is configured; no service state is changed.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Linux: terminal and distribution differences

Run the following only in an authorised Linux computer or VM. If you use Windows only, read this section for comparison. A program being absent does not mean the whole operating system is faulty.

Linux step 1 — Check what process is PID 1

ps -p 1 -o comm=

Expected result: Commonly prints systemd on systemd hosts; another name means follow that environment’s service model.

Linux step 2 — List currently running service units

systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager

Expected result: If systemd is available, displays units. Do not change or restart them during the exercise.

Linux step 3 — Inspect the state of a chosen unit

systemctl status --no-pager ssh.service

Expected result: ssh.service may have a different name or may not be installed. Use an actually listed service instead; status is a read-only probe.

Linux step 4 — Read only the last few journal messages

journalctl --no-pager -n 10

Expected result: Your permissions determine which messages are visible.

Worked support scenario

You are asked why a Linux training service did not start. First confirm whether the host uses systemd, then inspect the unit’s active state and the journal around the reported time. If the message says a configuration file is missing, do not create guessed settings in /etc. Report the specific path, the expected owner and the relevant documentation so the responsible maintainer can supply the approved configuration.

Common mistakes and safe responses

Mistake Better response
“systemctl enable starts a service immediately.” Enable changes activation relationships; use is-enabled or read documentation and distinguish it from start.
“Everything with a .service suffix is running.” A unit file may exist while the service is inactive or failed.
“No log output means no problem.” Journal permissions, filtering or retention can hide records.

Exercises

  1. Compare a service unit with an ordinary running process.

  2. On a Linux practice machine, list running units or record “systemd unavailable”.

  3. Identify what you would record before requesting a service restart.

Review questions and suggested answers

Show the suggested answers after attempting the exercises

  1. A unit adds configuration and lifecycle semantics; a process is a currently executing program.

  2. Either result is valid if supported by evidence.

  3. Service identity, status, reason for restart, observed error, expected impact, and rollback plan.

Chapter 29 · Intermediate

Chapter 29 — Plan software updates and understand the change window

Bits to Banking · System Administration: From Zero · Umicom Foundation

Audience: first-time users and returning learners; practical examples appropriate for supervised younger learners.

Estimated study time: 45–70 minutes.

Prerequisites: Chapters 8 and 23.

Why this matters

A package manager reports ten available updates. Installing all ten immediately might seem responsible, but a machine could be in the middle of an important class, a medical support session or a planned Umicom build. An administrator first identifies the change, verifies a backup and maintenance window, and understands what a rollback would require.

What you will be able to do

By the end of this chapter you should be able to explain the new terms in ordinary language, select a safe read-only command for the right operating system, recognise a normal result and identify an unverified result. You should also be able to describe what permission would be needed before making a real system change.

The mental model

A package manager tracks installed software and available packages. A security update fixes a vulnerability; a feature update may change behaviour; a driver or compiler update can invalidate assumptions about build reproducibility. The visible package list is not the whole software inventory: applications can be installed manually or managed by another provider. Upgrading software is a change with potential downstream effects. The correct rhythm is inventory → evaluate → obtain permission → prepare recovery → apply → verify → record. The first part of this lesson is deliberately read-only.

A deployment is not finished when an installer exits

A controlled upgrade needs a post-change acceptance test. For a text editor that might mean opening and saving a harmless document. For an Umicom Studio build environment it means checking compiler and linker versions, configuring the correct preset, building the expected targets and running the registered tests. A package manager exit code says whether its transaction succeeded; it does not prove that an unrelated dependent program still behaves correctly.

On a managed computer, administrators may pin versions, use central update policies or require maintenance windows. A beginner should not bypass those controls. It is also important to distinguish information collection from change. winget list --upgrade-available is observational. winget upgrade changes installed software. The latter belongs in a separate approved maintenance procedure with a recovery plan.

Words you should know

Term Meaning
Package manager Software that installs, upgrades or removes software packages.
Dependency Another package or library required by an application.
Change window An agreed time to apply changes with controlled impact.
Rollback Returning to a known working configuration after a failed change.
Compatibility matrix Recorded versions known to work together.

Windows: PowerShell 7, one command at a time

Use a normal non-elevated PowerShell window. Do not type the PS C:\...> prompt. If a command is unavailable or returns Access Denied, record that result; do not attempt to defeat the restriction.

The lines in a code block may contain more than one interactive command. Run them in order, checking each result before continuing. No .ps1 file is created or required.

Windows step 1 — Check the package manager version

winget --version

Expected result: A version number indicates Windows Package Manager is available; if unrecognised, consult the Windows installation guide.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 2 — List installed packages

winget list

Expected result: The result can be long and may include software installed through other methods.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 3 — List applications with available updates

winget list --upgrade-available

Expected result: Available updates are listed without installing them. A missing update is not proof the PC has no security issues.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Windows step 4 — Inspect one package’s metadata

winget show --id Git.Git --exact

Expected result: Package details and source are displayed when available; this is not an installation.

What this does: PowerShell runs the command in your current session and displays information or, where clearly indicated, changes only your own practice files. If output differs, record the actual result before going further.

Linux: terminal and distribution differences

Run the following only in an authorised Linux computer or VM. If you use Windows only, read this section for comparison. A program being absent does not mean the whole operating system is faulty.

Linux step 1 — Find the distribution

cat /etc/os-release

Expected result: Identifies the operating-system family; this file is normally world-readable.

Linux step 2 — List upgrade candidates on Debian/Ubuntu

apt list --upgradable

Expected result: Displays upgrade candidates from currently cached package metadata. The result can be stale until an authorised update refreshes it.

Linux step 3 — List installed OpenSSH package information (Debian/Ubuntu)

dpkg-query -W openssh-client

Expected result: Reports a version if installed, or a non-zero status if absent; do not assume all Linux uses dpkg.

Worked support scenario

The Umicom C23 laboratory compiled yesterday but fails after a compiler upgrade. Save the exact GCC, CMake and Ninja versions, the error log and the Git commit used. Before making further changes, check whether dependencies or compiler defaults have changed. A rollback of the compiler is a separate approved task; rewriting source without evidence can obscure the root cause.

Common mistakes and safe responses

Mistake Better response
“Run winget upgrade --all during the exercise.” That modifies real software and is not an observation; no updates are installed in this lab.
“A software update is always safe because it comes from a package manager.” Compatibility, trust, vendor support and rollback still need review.
“The package list is an immutable record.” Repositories and cached metadata change; note when and where the observation was taken.

Exercises

  1. Identify the difference between winget list --upgrade-available and winget upgrade.

  2. Write three checks you would make before updating a machine used for an Umicom demonstration.

  3. Record the currently installed version of one harmless development tool, without upgrading it.

Review questions and suggested answers

Show the suggested answers after attempting the exercises

  1. The first lists candidates; the second applies an update.

  2. Owner permission, current backup/recovery evidence, compatibility and timing are useful checks.

  3. For example, git --version or cmake --version records a version without changing software.
